content.title: About
content.content: Lunchmeat is a ready‑to‑eat roast beef that is thinly sliced and sealed in a vacuum‑packed pouch. It is made from selected cuts of beef that are roasted to a golden crust, cooled, and then sliced. The product is convenient for quick sandwiches, salads, and snack plates.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Roast beef is traditionally prepared from premium cuts such as the ribeye or sirloin.
Thinly sliced roast beef is a staple in many European dishes, including Swiss beef fondue.
Vacuum packaging extends shelf life without the need for artificial preservatives.
Roast beef can be served hot or cold while retaining its flavor and tenderness.
In the United States, roast beef is often seasoned further to create pastrami.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Roast beef provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Roast beef contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc in beef supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to beef.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepackaged roast beef often contains added salt for flavor and preservation.

items.title: Bacterial growth risk
items.content: Improper storage can allow pathogenic bacteria to proliferate.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Depending on the cut, the product may contain notable amounts of saturated fat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Roast beef can be eaten straight from the package, added to sandwiches, salads, wrapped in lettuce leaves, or incorporated into hot dishes such as pasta and casseroles. Thin slices make it an easy, protein‑rich snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepackaged roast beef in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3–5 days. If frozen, it can be kept for up to 2 months, though texture may decline.
